new_statements.translation: stress falls on the last syllable of the last root, regardless of the number of prefixes or roots before it, or of suffixes after it, as in (16). 16. [ʔa.mih.ki.ni.dip] ʔamik-i-ni-ti-p [3A] have.nightmares-INV-PERF-PL-NEU;INDEP 'they have had nightmares' (the '?' in the snippet is Google's rendering of ʔ)
new_statements.citation: Romero Méndez, Rodrigo. 2018. Apofonía no segmental en lenguas de la rama mixe. In Esther Herrera Zendejas & Verónica Reyes Taboada (eds.), Fonología segmental: procesos e interacciones, 47-83. México: El Colegio de México.
new_statements.locator: p. 16 of the Google Books ebook edition (id 0gKiDwAAQBAJ, 2019, 206 pp.), inside the section on verb-root classes just before example (16); print-edition page within pp. 47-83 not determined
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the last syllable of the last root of the word; prefixes and suffixes are ignored, so in a multi-root (compound/incorporating) word the final root carries stress and suffixes after it are unstressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in the captured snippet.
new_statements.domain_note: A family-level statement about Mixe languages (the chapter's data: Coatlán, Guichicovi, Mazatlán = Lowland; Alotepec, Ocotepec, San Isidro Huayapam = Midland; Ayutla, Tepuxtepec = South Highland; Totontepec = North Highland; Sayula and Oluta Popoluca), collected first-hand by the author; the example (16) is a verb form of unspecified variety (probably Ayutla). It is NOT a description of North Central Mixe specifically, and the sentence fixing its scope ('en las lenguas mixes...' or similar) could not be captured because Google Books blocked our machine after one in-book search. Domain is the morphological word; nothing said about phrase-level accent.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog nort2939 (North Central Mixe, neq) covers the North Midland towns Cotzocón, Puxmetacán, Jaltepec, Atitlán, Alotepec (dialect olot1240) and Zacatepec (zaca1240). The only target-specific description, Reyes Gómez 2009, is of Santa María Alotepec Mixe (olot1240). The one phonology thesis actually opened, Santos Martínez 2013 (San Miguel Metepec), turned out to be an agencia of Totontepec and is classed by its author as Mixe alto del norte, i.e. Totontepec Mixe [toto1304, mto], not this language (its moraic-trochee stress rule, pp. 228-236, belongs to the toto1304 entry). Wichmann 1995's Midland Mixe data are Cacalotepec and Juquila = Juquila Mixe [juqu1238]. The Romero Méndez 2018 statement quoted is family-level (Mixe branch), with Alotepec among the author's own data sets.

sources.citation: Santos Martínez, María del Rosario. 2013. El sistema fonológico del mixe de San Miguel Metepec: aspectos segmentales y prosódicos. Tesis de Maestría en Lingüística Indoamericana, CIESAS, México (dir. Francisco Arellanes). 254 pp. Open access, handle 1015/1111
sources.note: NOT THIS LANGUAGE: Metepec is an agencia of Totontepec Villa de Morelos (p. 3) and the author classes the variety as Mixe alto del norte (p. 4) = Totontepec Mixe [toto1304]. §4.4 pp. 228-236 gives a first-hand rule: moraic trochees from the right edge; final syllable with short/short-checked vowel -> penult stress; final syllable with long, long-checked or rearticulated vowel -> final stress (p. 234); 3 lexical exceptions (fn. 59, p. 233). Recorded here only as a mis-hit; useful for the toto1304 entry.
